description: If the same Excel or CSV report arrives every week, Power Query can record the cleanup steps once and repeat them on the next file with Refresh. This short shows the workflow and the validation step that should come after it. #excel #powerquery #automation #productivity

scenes.title: Same Excel cleanup every week?
scenes.note: Repeated clicks are a repeatable process.
scenes.narration: If the same Excel or CSV report arrives every week, stop treating the cleanup like a brand-new task.

scenes.title: Record the transformation once.
scenes.narration: In Power Query, build the transformation once. Remove unwanted rows, rename columns, set data types, and standardize the fields you actually understand.

scenes.title: Replace the source. Hit Refresh.
scenes.note: The steps run again in the same order.
scenes.narration: When the next file arrives in the same structure, replace the source and refresh. Power Query runs the same steps again in the same order.

scenes.title: Consistency beats repeated clicks.
scenes.narration: The real advantage is consistency. You are less likely to forget a step, and the transformation sequence stays visible.

scenes.title: Refresh is not the final step.
scenes.narration: After the refresh, validate the result. Compare row counts, check missing values, and make sure the expected columns are still there.

scenes.title: Recurring + structured = Power Query
scenes.narration: A useful rule is simple. One-time cleanup can stay in Excel. Recurring structured cleanup belongs in Power Query. More complex multi-file logic may belong in Python.
